modelOverview: Introduced in 1972 and designed by Gerald Genta, the Royal Oak was the first luxury sports watch in steel, defined by its octagonal bezel, eight hexagonal bezel screws and integrated bracelet. This grouping spans the wider Royal Oak family beyond the core 41mm Selfwinding line — from the discontinued 15400 predecessor and precious-metal 34/37mm 'mid-size' models to the 33mm Lady's automatic and quartz references — in steel, precious metals and ceramic.

15400OR.OO.D088CR.01.dial: Silver-toned 'Grande Tapisserie' dial with pink gold applied hour-markers and Royal Oak hands, date at 3 o'clock
15400OR.OO.D088CR.01.description: The Royal Oak Selfwinding 15400 was the direct predecessor to today's 15500/15510 family, produced from 2012 until its 2019 replacement. This pink gold example on a hand-stitched leather strap runs the in-house Calibre 3120 with roughly 60 hours of power reserve. Sourced and authenticated by our specialists.
